The Context

First marketer at a seed-stage agentic video editor

Osmo is an agentic video editor backed by Bain Capital Ventures: an end-to-end, fully editable video platform that gives storytellers complete authorship over the final result. I joined a seven-person team as the first and only dedicated marketer, owning positioning, pricing, launch, lifecycle, growth instrumentation, sales support, brand, and community.

Osmo Studio launch film
The Insight

The buyer is a creator, not a committee

Osmo was packaged for teams, but the people falling in love with it were individual designers, editors, and in-house creatives. They behave like consumers: they need to use the product before they upgrade or make the case to their team.

I reframed the buyer as an individual creator and positioned Osmo as editing and rendering in one place for design-savvy creatives. That insight became a $19 self-serve creator tier and an annual plan, the packaging's first individual entry point.

The Launch

Leading the public launch

I owned the launch campaign end to end: campaign design, media planning across micro-influencer seeding, all social channels, and press outreach with the investor's comms team.

  • Monthly new users grew 12x in launch month
  • MRR grew 4x in the first month post-launch
  • Co-organized SF Creatives Night, a 400+ registrant event that trended on Luma and drew investors and prospects

I also got my hands dirty on the creative: I co-wrote the script and ran camera on the pre-launch film ↗, kids at a skatepark trying agentic motion graphics for the first time, real reactions only.

I also co-led the launch redesign of osmo.inc ↗, owning the messaging track: the story the site tells from the hero to the pricing page, and how it hands off to the product.

Launch week across channels: X, Instagram, and LinkedIn, from founder posts to my own launch story
The Second Act

A launch only matters if it sticks

A launch spike is vanity unless it converts. After launch my focus shifted to lifecycle: nurturing the new cohort and turning trials into durable subscribers.

I designed the onboarding sequence: registration email, an A/B-tested activation email with an incentive offer, and a Discord community. The ongoing work is optimizing trial-to-paid conversion and the retention loops behind it.

Digging into what the new cohort was prompting for, combined with funnel analysis, I co-led new onboarding assets and template features with the product design team: a remix-first activation flow, so users who freeze at a blank canvas start from a template and make it theirs.

Activation email (Arm A of the A/B test): remix an animation instead of facing a blank canvas
New template and overlay features, co-designed with the product design team
Growth Infrastructure

Funnel data you can talk to

Working with an engineer, I built conversion tracking from zero: an end-to-end funnel from page view to paid, instrumented at the moments that matter for an agentic editor. Signup, trial start, first prompt, first export, upgrade. Each node is a place a creator can stall, so we can see where they drop, not just whether they convert.

On top of it we wired an agent query layer over the data warehouse, so the team can interrogate that funnel conversationally instead of working around GA's attribution gaps.

The agent lives in Slack as Kit Meow, the team's resident data cat: anyone can ask it funnel questions in plain language.

Kit Meow, the team’s agent in Slack. Fair question, someone actually asked for once.
Community

Building the room, not just the funnel

Growth at Osmo is community-shaped. I co-hosted SF Creatives Night: Hard Launch x Osmo, a screening night for creatives in tech who are artists first. It drew 400+ registrants, was featured on Luma San Francisco, and filled the room with prospects and investors.

SF Creatives Night: Hard Launch x Osmo, July 30, 2026
Co-hosted with the Osmo and Hard Launch teams
Featured among Luma’s popular events in San Francisco

Beyond events, I built and run the Osmo Discord as the home for creators onboarding to the product, and I am producing a customer feedback video series and asset library so real users tell the product story in their own words.

On the Ground

Selling it myself

I carried an AE role on client engagements to learn how the product lands in production work, and independently ran the product portion of sales calls, using live demos to pressure-test features before launch.
